put.description: Sets the controller endpoint, optional data route base and optional write-only bearer credential (kept when omitted, removed by clearCredential). Availability defaults to all universes on creation and is preserved when omitted on update. The controller is probed: a definitive refusal is invalidRequest, unreachable is accepted.

schema.description:
Register or replace a provider. `credential` is the optional bearer
token Lightspeed presents to the provider's controller and data routes:
it is sealed on receipt and never returned by any method. `Debug` output
redacts it; request logging must never echo these params.

availableToAllUniverses.description:
Allow every universe to use the provider. Set to `false` to require a binding.
Omit to keep the current setting. New providers default to `true`.

controllerEndpoint.description: `ws://`, `wss://` or `unix://` URL of the provider controller.

credential.description:
A new bearer credential; omit to keep the stored one. A provider needs
none. Excludes `clearCredential`.

dataRouteBase.description:
`ws://` or `wss://` base of the provider's data routes; omit to derive
it from the controller endpoint. Required for a `unix://` controller,
and must not be `ws://` for a `wss://` controller.

get.description: Returns deployment-wide summaries, including metadata, protection, expiry and deleting universes. The metadata filter requires every supplied key/value pair. Aggregate counts and last session activity are approximate.

schema.description: Return universes containing every supplied key/value pair.

post.description: Creates a universe for an explicit UUID with optional handle, metadata, protection and future expiry. Protection and expiry are mutually exclusive. Idempotent: existing universes retain all settings. A claimed handle or deleting/deleted UUID returns conflict.

expiresAtMs.description: Future Unix time in milliseconds. Incompatible with protection.

handle.description:
The new universe's handle: 1-63 lowercase letters, digits and
hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit, and not in the
form of a UUID. Omit it to have one derived from the UUID. Ignored
when the universe already exists.

metadata.description:
At most 32 string entries; keys up to 64 bytes, values up to 256 bytes.
Caller keys cannot start with lightspeed.

delete.description: Refuses protected universes. Immediately fences an unprotected universe and releases its handle. A background worker removes schedules, workflows, environments, objects and rows. Repeated requests return deleting or deleted; unknown IDs return notFound.

get.description: Returns one deployment tenant summary, addressed by UUID or active handle, with aggregate session, workspace, profile, and blob usage. Deleting universes remain readable by UUID. A permanently deleted UUID returns gone with its deletion record; an unknown UUID returns notFound.

post.description: Decodes and stores a batch of base64 payloads, returning immutable content references in request order. Re-uploading identical bytes is naturally deduplicated.

schema.description:
`blobs/put` is batch-native: pass one item to store a single blob. Results
come back in request order. Uploads are eligible for collection after the
deployment's grace period unless retained by a durable resource. Reads do
not extend retention; admitting an existing ref refreshes its grace.

get.description: Checks a batch of content references without returning blob bodies, preserving request order.
Streams immutable blob bytes from this universe. Content-Length reports the complete representation size. Range requests are not supported.

put.description: Streams bytes into immutable universe storage. The path is the expected content digest; Content-Length is required and both length and digest are verified. An identical upload is idempotent. Admission refreshes the blob's collection grace period.

get.description: Returns the roster: every bot with its trigger count, pending event count, and latest event, optionally narrowed by createdBy.

post.description: Creates the bot record, optionally with its triggers, and starts its controller. Fails if the bot id exists; a trigger failure rolls the bot back. Returns the created webhook triggers' ingest paths by trigger id.

triggers.description:
Triggers created with the bot in one go; a failure rolls the bot
back.

delete.description: Closes the bot if needed, waits for its controller to complete, retains its session history, and removes the record so the bot id is free again.

get.description: Returns the bot record, its current revision, and lifecycle columns.

put.description: Replaces the mutable configuration whole and signals the controller, which applies it at its next idle boundary. Pass expectedRevision when replacing; a closed bot accepts label-only edits.

bot.description:
The mutable configuration of a bot, replaced whole with an expected
revision. The bot id, event counter, and lifecycle columns live on the
record, not here.

brief.description:
Standing instructions appended to the profile's instructions — the
bot's job description.

description.description: One line other bots read in the directory.

displayName.description: Mutable label for humans; the bot id stays the identity.

emit.description:
Capability grant: `bot_emit` — events to itself or another bot's
inbox. Emitting bots are rate-capped.

enabled.description:
Reversible pause: sessions and chat context stay, nothing is
delivered.

routedSessionCloseAfterMs.description:
Close routed (`perKey` / `perEvent`) sessions idle longer than this;
absent keeps them open. A trigger's `sessionCloseAfterMs` overrides it.

runsPerDay.description:
Budget: runs started per UTC day (sub-agent descendants count);
absent means unlimited.

selfConfig.description:
Capability grant: the mutating self-configuration tools
(`bot_trigger_put`, `bot_trigger_delete`, `bot_brief_put`).

expectedRevision.description:
Checked only when the bot already exists; absent replaces (or
creates) unconditionally.

put.summary: Create or replace a bot document

post.description: Terminal and idempotent: disables every trigger, drops schedules, and tells the controller to archive pending events and force-close its sessions. Returns once signalled; follow bots/state/read for closing to closed.

get.description: Cursor-paginated event log, newest first, with outcomes; payload documents stay in the CAS.

schema.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page.

post.description: Stores an operator-authored event for the bot's main session and wakes the controller. eventId is the dedupe identity; a duplicate returns the stored row.

get.description: Returns the event row and its full stored envelope document.

post.description: Re-admits the stored envelope as a fresh event with the original routing; the replay never coalesces.
Evaluates a filter against one payload or a sample of recent stored events, reporting matches and evaluation errors without changing anything.

limit.description: How many recent stored events to sample when no payload is given.

payload.description:
A document to test instead of stored events: `{kind?, data?,
headers?}`.

post.description: Asks the controller to close one of the bot's sessions at its next idle boundary and continue on a fresh generation; queued deliveries follow.

sessionId.description:
One of the bot's sessions (main or routed); the controller closes it
at its next idle boundary and continues on a successor generation.

get.description: Queries the controller workflow for its live snapshot (sessions, buffers, active and recent deliveries, budget) and lists sub-agent descendants. The controller is absent until the bot's first event.
Returns every trigger of the bot ordered by id, without ingest paths.

delete.description: Drops the trigger's Temporal Schedule, then the record; stored events keep their history.

get.description: Returns one trigger with its incidents and cursor. Read a webhook's ingest path through bots/triggers/secrets/read.

put.description: Validates the trigger document (CEL parses, grants exist, one inbox per bot), reconciles its Temporal Schedule, and stores it. A poll spec edit resets the cursor; a webhook keeps its URL token. Returns a webhook's ingest path beside the view.

expectedRevision.description:
Checked only when the trigger already exists; absent replaces (or
creates) unconditionally.

trigger.description:
The whole configuration of one trigger, replaced with an expected
revision.

atMs.description: One-shot instant; the trigger disables itself after firing.

cron.description: Classic 5-field cron or an `@macro`; exclusive with `atMs`.

summary.description: What the fired event asks the session to do.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for cron evaluation; default `UTC`.

items.description:
Dot path to the item array in the payload; absent = the payload
is the item list (or one item).

oneOf.description:
Inbox: which bots may address this one; absent = any bot in the
universe.

filter.description:
CEL over `{event, data, headers}`; a non-matching event is refused
and never stored. Fails closed.

sessionCloseAfterMs.description:
Idle-close policy for sessions this trigger routes to: absent inherits the
bot's `routedSessionCloseAfterMs`, `0` keeps them open indefinitely.

get.description: Returns the webhook ingest path. Its token lets the holder post events to the bot. Requires bot-management permission.

put.description: Updates supplied displayName, metadata and protected. Omitted fields retain their values; metadata replaces the complete map. Protection refuses deletion and cannot coexist with an expiry. Clearing protection is explicit and never implied by deletion.

schema.description: Patch universe settings. Absent fields retain their values.

metadata.description: Replaces the complete metadata map; omission leaves it unchanged.

protected.description: Deletion is refused while enabled. Cannot be enabled while an expiry exists.

get.description: Lists non-secret OAuth client registrations in the universe.

post.description: Stores provider endpoints and client identity; an optional plaintext client secret is encrypted and represented thereafter only by hasClientSecret.

schema.description:
Register an OAuth client configuration. `client_secret` is the second
deliberate inbound-plaintext path after `credentials/grants/import`: it is
encrypted on receipt and never returned by any method. `Debug` output
redacts it; request logging must never echo these params.

delete.description: Deletes the client registration and its stored client secret; grants already created from it remain separate records.

get.description: Returns endpoints, public client identity, defaults, and secret-presence state; the client secret is never returned.

post.description: Creates a short-lived PKCE flow carrying the immutable grant exposure choice and returns a browser authorization URL containing one-time state. Treat the URL as sensitive and poll credentials/flows/read for completion.

get.description: Polls a flow's pending/completed/failed/expired state and returns the resulting grant id when authorization succeeds; no token value is exposed.
Lists non-secret grant metadata for the universe, optionally filtered by status.

post.description: Accepts a plaintext token, encrypts it immediately, and returns only grant metadata/token-presence flags. Brokered is the default; exposure is immutable, and only a retrievable credential can be leased to a service or bound into an environment.

schema.description:
Import a new token credential as a credential grant, under the given id or an
allocated one; an id already in use is a conflict. Together with
[`CredentialGrantPutParams`] this is the deliberate inbound-plaintext path:
`token` is encrypted on receipt and is never returned by any method. `Debug` output redacts the token; request
logging must never echo these params.

metadata.description:
Non-secret, caller-defined metadata stored on the grant and returned
by reads (for example which product a pasted subscription token
belongs to). Must be a JSON object; never put secret material here.

get.description: Returns creator attribution, provider binding, scopes, audience, expiry, status, and token-presence flags; access and refresh token values are never returned.

put.description: Makes the token credential of this id exist with these settings and hold exactly the supplied token, encrypted on receipt. Repeating it changes nothing. A missing credential is created; a different token replaces the stored one for everything referencing the id. Conflict: another kind of grant, a revoked one, or changed exposure.

schema.description:
Declare a token credential (`staticToken`): its id, its settings and the
token it holds. A credential that is missing is created. One that exists
has its settings replaced by these (an absent field is unset) and, when it
holds a different token, that token replaced, so MCP servers, headers,
bot polls and environment variables referencing the id use the new value
from their next request or process. Declaring it again changes nothing.

`token` is encrypted on receipt and never returned; `Debug` output redacts
it and request logging must never echo these params.

dryRun.description: Report what the declaration would do without doing it.

expiresAtMs.description: When the token expires. Absent means it does not expire.

exposure.description:
Whether the plain token may be leased to a service or bound into an
environment. It cannot be changed afterwards.

metadata.description:
Non-secret, caller-defined metadata. Must be a JSON object; never put
secret material here.

providerId.description:
Label recorded on the credential; `static` when absent. It cannot be
changed afterwards.

post.description: Service callers only. Resolves the current access token through the broker, records the lease, and returns it once. Cache only in memory until expiry minus margin (or at most five minutes without expiry), re-lease after target 401/403, and never persist or place the token in workflow payloads.

schema.description:
Request a current access-token lease for a retrievable grant. Callers must
cache only in memory until shortly before `expiresAtMs` (or for at most
five minutes when it is absent), re-lease after target 401/403 responses,
and never persist the token or place it in a workflow payload.

post.description: Marks the grant unusable by token consumers while retaining non-secret audit metadata.

get.description: Lists non-secret model/GitHub provider registrations for the universe.

post.description: Creates a model or GitHub credential source. Plaintext API keys/private keys are encrypted on receipt and later represented only by configuration plus hasCredential.

schema.description:
Register a credential provider. `credential` (for GitHub Apps: the private
key PEM) is the third deliberate inbound-plaintext path: it is encrypted
on receipt and never returned by any method. `Debug` output redacts it;
request logging must never echo these params.

delete.description: Deletes the provider registration and its directly stored credential; separately stored grants remain independent records.

get.description: Returns provider kind, non-secret configuration, credential-presence state, and status; stored credentials are never returned.

put.description: Makes the provider of this id exist with this configuration and credential. Repeating it changes nothing. A missing provider is created; one that differs is rewritten in place after the new settings validate, atomically, and its old credential deleted. Sessions and environment variables referencing the id keep working.

schema.description:
Declare a provider: its id, its configuration and its credential. A
provider that is missing is created. One that exists is rewritten in place
as if it were created again under the same id, where it differs: the new
settings are validated before anything changes, so a rejected declaration
leaves the provider as it was, and sessions and environment variables
referencing the id keep working throughout. Declaring it again changes
nothing. `credential` is encrypted on receipt and never returned; `Debug`
output redacts it.

credential.description:
The provider's credential, for the kinds that take one. Absent leaves
the provider without a credential.

dryRun.description: Report what the declaration would do without doing it.

get.description: Uses the registered GitHub App provider credential to query accessible installations and returns account/permission metadata without tokens.

post.description: Creates or refreshes a universe credential grant for one accessible installation. This method never returns a token: the broker mints short-lived installation tokens when the grant is used. Brokered is the default; only a grant created retrievable can be bound into an environment or leased to a service.
post.summary: Grant access to a GitHub App installation

get.description: Administrative metadata for soft-deleted sessions, ordered by session ID. Unavailable through universe-scoped methods.

schema.description: Exclusive session ID cursor; each page contains at most 100 entries.

delete.description: Removes a soft-deleted session and its soft-deleted history subtree. Rejects any selected session that has not been soft-deleted. Releases event, checkpoint and blob references; unreferenced blobs follow normal garbage collection. Does not delete external workspaces, environments, backups or Temporal history.

get.description: Deployment configuration inventory of one universe's provider bindings.
get.summary: List a universe's deployment provider bindings

delete.description: Stops a universe from using a provider that is not available to all universes. Its open environments on the provider lose access until it is bound again.

put.description: Allows one universe to use a deployment provider that is not available to all universes. Repeating it changes nothing.

schema.description:
Allow a universe to use a provider that is not available to all
universes. Repeating it changes nothing; for a provider available to all
universes it has no effect.

get.description: Reads selected job handles with bounded output from a byte offset or the output tail; continue from each entry's outputNext and poll on the returned status.

schema.description:
Byte offset to read each job's output from: a previous entry's
`outputNext`. Omitted with `tailBytes` omitted reads from the start.
Most output bytes per job; omit for the server's default page.
Read each job's last `tailBytes` of output instead; excludes `after`.

post.description: Requests cancellation for selected jobs, optionally including dependents. Force is provider-specific escalation; inspect each per-job result.

get.description: Lists the deployment providers this universe may create environments from: those available to every universe, and those this universe is bound to.
Returns one provider this universe may create environments from; not found when it may not. Templates and physical resource, network, and ingress policy remain provider-owned.
Reads templates live from the controllers of every provider available to the universe, or of one provider: compute, power states, public ingress, and default idle policy.

schema.description:
Only this provider's templates; omit for every provider available to
the universe.

get.description: Returns one template, read live from the controller of a provider available to the universe.
Lists this universe's registration keys with policy, status, and derived counts. Each key is the group of the environments it admitted.

post.description: Creates a reusable universe-scoped key that lets outbound envd daemons register as environments. The plaintext secret is returned exactly once; only its hash is stored. Identity mode (immutable), active limit, disconnect grace, offline close-after, and expiry are the key's policy. Treat the secret like a cluster-join credential.

declaredOnly.description:
Persistent keys only: admit only daemons whose registration name
matches an environment declared under this key.

displayName.description: Group name for the environments this key admits.

ephemeralDisconnectGraceMs.description: Disconnect grace for ephemeral environments; omit for the default.

maxActiveEnvironments.description: Non-closed environments the key may have at once; omit for unlimited.

offlineCloseAfterMs.description:
Persistent keys only: close environments whose daemon has been away
longer than this; omit to keep them open.

registrationKeyId.description:
The key's id within the universe: 1-128 ASCII letters, digits,
underscores, hyphens, dots or colons, starting with a letter or digit.
Omit it to have one allocated.

get.description: Returns the key's display prefix, policy, status, and derived environment counts; never the secret or its hash.

patch.description: Replaces a key's editable policy: display name, active limit, disconnect grace, offline close-after, and expiry; an omitted field is unset. The identity mode is immutable. The active limit and expiry apply to later admissions; a changed disconnect grace or offline close-after applies at the next sweep to environments whose daemon is away.

schema.description:
The complete editable policy of a registration key; an absent field is
unset. The identity mode is immutable.

declaredOnly.description:
Persistent keys only: admit only daemons whose registration name
matches an environment declared under this key.

displayName.description: Group name for the environments this key admits.

ephemeralDisconnectGraceMs.description: Disconnect grace for ephemeral environments; omit for the default.

maxActiveEnvironments.description: Non-closed environments the key may have at once; omit for unlimited.

offlineCloseAfterMs.description:
Persistent keys only: close environments whose daemon has been away
longer than this; omit to keep them open.

put.description: Makes the key of this id exist with this policy and answer to exactly the supplied secret. Repeating it changes nothing. A missing key is created; a different secret retires the previous one at once, as rotation does. Conflict: a changed identity mode, a revoked key, or a secret that is or was a key's.

schema.description:
Declare a registration key whose secret the caller supplies: its id, its
complete policy and the secret it answers to. An absent policy field is
unset.

declaredOnly.description:
Persistent keys only: admit only daemons whose registration name
matches an environment declared under this key.

displayName.description: Group name for the environments this key admits.

ephemeralDisconnectGraceMs.description: Disconnect grace for ephemeral environments; omit for the default.

maxActiveEnvironments.description: Non-closed environments the key may have at once; omit for unlimited.

offlineCloseAfterMs.description:
Persistent keys only: close environments whose daemon has been away
longer than this; omit to keep them open.

secret.description:
The secret daemons register with: `lsrk_` followed by 32 random bytes
encoded as base64url without padding. Generate it with a
cryptographic random source.

post.description: Stops the key from admitting new daemon identities; already registered daemons keep reconnecting. With closeEnvironments, also closes every non-closed environment the key admitted. Idempotent.

closeEnvironments.description: Also close every non-closed environment the key admitted.

post.description: Replaces the key's secret and display prefix and retires the old secret at once. The key keeps its id, group, policy, and the environments it admitted; daemons already registered are unaffected because they never present the key again. Returns the new secret once. Refused for a revoked key.

get.description: Lists the universe environments in id order, one page at a time, optionally filtered by provider, registration key, state, or metadata. Closed environments are omitted unless includeClosed is set or state is closed. Continue from nextAfter.

schema.description: Exclusive environment id cursor: a previous page's `nextAfter`.
Also list closed environments; they are omitted by default.
Most environments per page; omit for 100.

Only environments carrying every listed metadata pair (AND
semantics); the same filter `session/list` accepts.
Only provisioned environments of this provider.
Only registered environments admitted by this registration key.

Only environments in this lifecycle state. `closed` lists closed
environments without `includeClosed`.

post.description: Creates a provisioned environment, attributed to the caller, from a template of a provider enabled for the universe. Idempotent per requestId: same inputs, same environment; others conflict. Provisioning until the target's first envd handshake, then open; idle overrides the template default.

environmentId.description:
The id profiles and bindings use for the environment. Omit it to have
one allocated. An id already in use is a conflict.

idle.description:
Idle policy passed to the provider in place of the template's `idle`.
The provider runs the idle clock; it cannot be changed after create.

providerId.description:
The provider to create the environment with; it must be available to
the universe.

requestId.description:
Stable caller-generated retry identity, unique inside the universe.
Retrying with identical inputs returns the same environment.

templateId.description: The provider template to create the environment from.

get.description: Returns one environment: its source, lifecycle state, derived display status, state message, close reason, daemon build, and the latest provider observation.

patch.description: Replaces the display name and caller metadata of an environment of any kind. Refused for a closed environment.

schema.description: Replace an environment's display name and caller metadata.

displayName.description: The new display name; omit to clear it.

metadata.description: The complete new caller metadata; omit or `{}` to clear it.

post.description: Closes an environment; idempotent. A provisioned environment moves to closing while Lightspeed asks its provider to remove the target, retrying until it is gone, then closed. External and registered environments close at once, and a connected registered daemon is told its environment closed.

get.description: Returns variable names and credential source handles for a universe environment; resolved secret values are never returned.

delete.description: Removes one variable-to-credential mapping without deleting the underlying grant or provider credential.

put.description: Maps an environment variable name to a retrievable credential grant or to a model API key provider's stored key. Commands in the environment receive the plain value, so a brokered grant and any other provider credential are refused. Requires configuring resources in the universe. The response exposes only the source handle, never secret material.
put.summary: Bind a credential into an environment

put.description: Synchronously ensures or removes public ingress of an open provisioned environment through its provider; source.publicEndpoint carries the reported endpoint. Rejected when the provider offers no ingress; an internal error, safe to retry, when the provider is unreachable or times out. The provider owns hostname, guest port, routing, TLS, and health.

enabled.description: Ensure (`true`) or remove (`false`) the provider's public ingress.

post.description: Starts a dependency-aware job group on one environment instance, injecting its configured credentials at provider start. requestId is the retry identity; jobs are owned by the instance, not a session. A powered-down environment wakes on its data route; the call fails with environmentNotReady while it wakes or reconnects; retry with backoff.

put.description: Synchronously moves an open provisioned environment's target to running, paused, suspended, or stopped via its provider and records the observation; the provider may also change power on idle. Rejected without provider power control or when the template lacks the state; an internal error, safe to retry, when the provider is unreachable or times out.

power.description:
Power state to move the target to; one of its template's
`powerStates`.

put.description: Declares a fixed machine as an open environment with a chosen id before its daemon registers. The first daemon its persistent key admits under the given name is bound to it; until then it is away and tools wait. Repeating it changes nothing; display name and metadata converge. The key and name are fixed. Conflict: an id or name in use.

schema.description: The id profiles and bindings use for the environment.

Declare a fixed machine as an environment before its daemon registers.
The first daemon the key admits under `name` becomes this environment and
keeps its id; from then on only that daemon's identity reconnects to it.

name.description:
The name the daemon registers under: 1 to 128 bytes without control
characters, unique among the open environments of the key. It cannot
be changed afterwards.

registrationKeyId.description:
The persistent registration key whose daemons may fill it. It cannot
be changed afterwards.

post.description: Forgets the daemon bound to a declared environment and ends its connection, so another daemon identity may bind under the same key and name. The environment keeps its id, its name, its credential bindings and every reference to it. No effect when no daemon is bound. Refused for an environment that was not declared.

schema.description:
Forget the daemon bound to a declared environment so that another
identity may bind to it.

get.description: Requires Accept: text/event-stream. Emits list rows after a short batching window, starting with watch/reset. Refetch on reset and periodically: signals can be lost. Ends after 15 minutes; reconnect to reauthenticate. Includes sub-agents; visibleTo restricts session access as on session/list.

schema.description: Collections to watch; omission selects all four. Must be nonempty.

Restrict session rows to shared sessions and sessions created by this actor,
as on session/list. Includes delegated children through their root's access.
Named SSE events. Each data field contains that notification's params object, without an outer envelope.

put.description: Sets a future Unix timestamp or clears expiry with explicit null. Protected universes cannot have an expiry. Expiry starts the normal deletion process, attributed to the runtime; activity does not extend it.

schema.description: Replace or clear expiry. Explicit null clears it; omission is refused.

post.description: Creates an open environment backed by a Lightspeed-reachable envd endpoint, attributed to the caller. Idempotent per requestId. Reachability is checked on use.

endpoint.description:
`ws://`, `wss://` or `unix://` URL of an envd instance reachable from
Lightspeed.

environmentId.description:
The id profiles and bindings use for the environment. Omit it to have
one allocated. An id already in use is a conflict.

requestId.description: Stable caller-generated retry identity, unique inside the universe.

put.description: Changes the deployment-unique handle without changing the universe UUID or resources. The previous handle is released: requests and URLs that use it stop reaching this universe, and another universe may claim it. Claiming another universe's handle returns a conflict. Does not create a universe.

schema.description: The universe's UUID or current handle.

Rename a universe. The UUID and resources remain unchanged; the previous
handle is released, so requests and URLs using it stop reaching this
universe.

handle.description:
The new handle: 1-63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting
and ending with a letter or digit, and not in the form of a UUID.

post.description: Looks for standards-based OAuth protected-resource metadata without creating a server, OAuth client, flow, or grant. An absent OAuth result is inconclusive and callers must allow manual auth selection.

schema.description:
Read-only authentication discovery for a prospective MCP endpoint. A
missing OAuth result is deliberately inconclusive: the server may be
public, use bearer auth, or expose OAuth metadata only through an explicit
URL. No catalog or auth records are created by this probe.

get.description: Lists the universe catalog entries, optionally filtered by lifecycle/configuration status.

delete.description: Deletes the catalog document. Existing session configs that reference it are not silently rewritten and may need explicit reconfiguration.

get.description: Returns one catalog document with defaults, auth policy, non-secret grant binding, status, and revision; no credential value is exposed.

put.description: Stores the complete catalog document with its optional credential grant. A new server is attributed to the caller. Use expectedRevision when replacing; token material is never accepted or returned, but serverUrl is stored and shown as written, so keep secrets out of it.

expectedRevision.description:
Checked only when the server already exists; absent replaces (or
creates) unconditionally.

server.description: Full MCP server document as submitted by clients.

approval.description: Approval policy for every session linking this server.

deferLoading.description: Provider-side deferred loading of tool definitions where supported.

headers.description:
Extra request headers sent on every request to the server, alongside
any `Authorization` the auth policy produces. Names are
case-insensitive and stored lowercased; transport headers,
`authorization` and `x-lightspeed-*` are reserved. `api-key` and
`x-api-key` carry a secret and accept only a `credential` value.
Requires `runtime` execution.

put.summary: Create or replace an MCP server record

post.description: Connects directly to the configured MCP server with its current universe credential and returns one bounded live tools/list result. The inventory is never persisted or cached and no tool is invoked.

schema.description: Live, non-persisting tool discovery for a configured MCP server.

get.description: Returns the revision and independent agentRun and speechToText selections. Revision zero means no update has been made. Does not contact model providers.

put.description: Sets or explicitly clears one purpose slot. With expectedRevision the write is refused if the defaults changed since. Existing sessions and admitted work keep their model. Validates the purpose and protocol without contacting provider discovery.

expectedRevision.description:
Write only if the defaults are still at this revision, as returned by
read or put; zero for a universe with no updates. Omit it to write
whatever the current revision is.

model.description: Complete selection, or explicit null to clear this slot. Required.

get.description: Queries supported providers directly, with a brief process-local burst cache, and returns best-effort selectable routes. One provider failure does not discard successful results from others.

schema.description:
Apply Lightspeed's small, conservative selectable-model policy. It
keeps supported file-transcription routes and filters clearly unrelated
OpenAI families from agent suggestions (embeddings, moderation, image/video,
speech synthesis, and realtime). Agent suggestions also have an age limit.
Clients select routes by API kind for their intended use. This is an ID
policy, not a provider capability claim.

get.description: Returns lightweight summaries of universe-scoped reusable profiles.

post.description: Creates a new universe-scoped reusable profile document; use profiles/put for create-or-replace revision semantics.

delete.description: Deletes the catalog document; sessions previously created or configured from it retain their materialized state.

get.description: Returns the complete profile document and current revision.

put.description: Stores the complete profile document. Use expectedRevision from profiles/read when replacing to prevent lost updates; absence writes unconditionally.

expectedRevision.description:
Checked only when the profile already exists; absent replaces (or
creates) unconditionally.

metadata.description:
Descriptive metadata defaults copied to a session when it is created
from this profile. Explicit `session/start` metadata wins key by key.
Applying the profile to an existing session does not change metadata.

retention.description:
Creation-time session retention default. Absence keeps the tree until
manual deletion. Applying a profile to an existing session does not
change retention.

put.summary: Create or replace an agent profile

get.description: Returns a cursor-paginated summary list ordered by most recent update, optionally narrowed by filters such as visibleTo, which keeps sessions whose root is shared with the universe or was created by that actor. An unknown parameter is refused. Pages may shift while sessions are changing.

schema.description:
Only closed sessions (`true`), or only new and open ones (`false`).
Absent lists both. Every filter here narrows the list, and an absent
one does not filter.
Opaque cursor from the previous page's `nextCursor`.

Only work whose root a lifecycle controller owns (`true`), or work no
controller owns (`false`); sub-agents follow their root. Absent lists
both.

Only sessions matching every entry (AND semantics). A non-empty value
requires an exact key/value pair; an empty value requires key presence.
Only sub-agent sessions this session delegated directly.

Only sub-agent sessions (`true`), or only root sessions (`false`).
Absent lists both.
Only these root sessions and all their sub-agents.

Only sessions whose root is shared with the universe or was created
by this actor: what that actor sees as a non-administrator.

post.description: Creates a session, unshared unless access says universe, with optional config, profile and immutable integration. Explicit values override profile metadata and retention; the default environment attachment becomes active. Retrying an id returns it and restarts a stopped execution from its log, unless integrated. Failed setup closes a server-allocated id.

access.description:
Audience of the new session, set atomically with its creation. Absent
means unshared until `session/share`; a retry keeps the original.

deleteAfterCloseMs.description:
Root-owned automatic soft deletion measured from close. Absent inherits a
profile default, explicit null keeps the tree, and a duration overrides
the profile.

integration.description:
Immutable lifecycle controller and workflow tools connecting this session
to outside workflows, admitted only when it is first created, with bound
dispatch stated explicitly. This document is not part of `SessionConfig`
and cannot be changed through `session/config/put`. Retrying an id with an
integration requires the same one, and a session started without one
cannot gain one. Any retry of an integrated session answers
`sessionExecutionStopped` for a stopped workflow execution instead of
restarting it.

metadata.description:
Descriptive key/value metadata, applied only when the session is
first created: at most 32 entries, keys 1..=64 bytes, values 1..=256
bytes, no control characters, no `lightspeed.` prefix. It never
affects routing, authority, or selection; filter on it with
`session/list`.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a closed retention-tree leaf, or its closed delegated-child subtree when cascade is true. Set softDelete to true to hide sessions while retaining records and history until a deployment administrator purges them. Prior soft deletion is not required for permanent deletion.

schema.description:
Delete delegated descendants too. False requires the target to be a
closed retention-tree leaf.

Atomically require every selected session's audience to be shared.
Delegating services use this guard for operators deleting shared work.

Hide sessions while retaining records, events, checkpoints and blob roots.
False (the default) permanently deletes them without prior soft deletion.

get.description: Returns stored state plus a bounded newest-first run-summary page, and needs no worker. An open session whose execution has stopped reports executionFailure. Follow nextRunCursor with session/runs/list when hasOlderRuns is true; use session/events/read for the transcript.

schema.description:
Newest run summaries to include. Values above the server maximum are
clamped.

delete.description: Clears active environment selection without changing or closing the universe environment.

put.description: Selects an attached, live universe environment for environment-targeted tools while the session is idle.

post.description: Closes an idle session and detaches its environment bindings. Without force, active work of any kind, including a pending detached promise, rejects the call. Force mode cancels active work, drops queued runs, and can recover a session whose workflow is unavailable.

force.description:
Cancel the active run and drop queued runs instead of rejecting on
active work. Recovers sessions whose workflow no longer exists (e.g.
after an operator terminate) by reconciling the session log directly. A
session that never opened has no log to close, so it is removed and the
call answers `notFound`.

put.description: Replaces the complete sparse config while the session is idle. Use the current config revision for safe read-modify-write; omitted features are revoked, an omitted model preserves the current model, and an identical document is a no-op. A newly attached MCP server must be usable; a held one that has gone away only drops out of later runs.

schema.description:
Replace the session config with a complete document. Anything omitted
from the document reverts to defaults; an absent feature is revoked.
Requires an idle session; putting an identical document is a no-op that
leaves the revision untouched.

expectedConfigRevision.description:
Checked against the session's current config revision when present;
absent replaces unconditionally.

post.description: Admits a batch of keyed context entries with per-entry results. The same content under a key is a no-op. Different content replaces the earlier entry, which leaves active context, and goes last under a new id; a catalog supersedes instead. Invalid input can fail one entry without discarding successful entries.

Performs one standalone compaction in any automatic mode, including Disabled, and waits for its outcome. Active work queues it until a safe turn boundary. A failed compaction leaves the context unchanged and fails the call with its reason. A wait that runs out fails with operationPending while it can still complete; session events report the outcome.
Removes active entries by stable key with per-key results. Missing keys are idempotent no-ops; runtime-reserved run keys cannot be removed.

keys.description:
Active context keys to remove. Removing a key that is already absent
is a per-key no-op (`absent`), so retries are idempotent. Keys under
reserved namespaces (`run`, `run.*`, `runtime`, `runtime.*`) are rejected
request-level.

post.description: Replaces active tool results and user messages in place by entry id, with per-entry results, e.g. to withdraw content the provider rejects. Entries keep their ids, positions, and kinds, so a tool result takes only text and its call stays answered. Refused while a run is active; ids no longer in context report absent.

get.description: Returns chronological events. Forward (default) follows after and supports long-polling. Backward reads the latest window below before (or the head); pass nextCursor as before until complete. Follow live events after the initial backward headCursor. Windows may split runs/tool batches; keep historical reconstruction separate from live controls.

schema.description: Exclusive upper sequence bound for backward reads only. Must be positive.

Forward reads follow `after`; backward reads select the latest window
below `before` (or the current head when absent). Both return events
chronologically. Backward reads do not replay reducer state.

Forward reads only. Long-poll: when no events exist past `after`, hold the request until
one lands or this many milliseconds elapse, then return a normal
(possibly empty) page. Zero or absent preserves immediate return.
Values above the server cap are clamped, not rejected.

put.description: Replaces the complete descriptive key/value map (bounded like session/start); an omitted or empty map clears it. Record-only: the event log and updatedAtMs are untouched.

schema.description:
Replace a session's metadata with a complete map (the same bounds as
`session/start`). Record-only: it does not touch the event log or
`updatedAtMs`. There is no merge form; read, edit, and put.

metadata.description: The complete new map; empty clears it.

put.description: Sets the display name, or clears it when displayName is omitted.

displayName.description: New display name; absent clears it. Cannot contain NUL.

post.description: Applies a named or inline profile's config, instructions, and environment setup to an existing session; mutating profile sections require it to be open and idle. Pass current revisions to guard concurrent changes.
post.summary: Apply a profile to a session

post.description: Starts a new workflow execution for an open session whose last one stopped, from its log. A run that was not parked fails, a parked run keeps waiting, and queued runs start afterwards. A running session is left alone. Refused for a closed session and for one with no run history.

put.description: Sets the positive close-relative automatic soft-deletion duration on a retention root, or clears it with null. Delegated children inherit the root policy and cannot override it. Retention does not permanently delete stored history.

deleteAfterCloseMs.description: Positive duration enables automatic tree soft deletion; null disables it.

get.description: Returns a newest-first keyset page of bounded run summaries, from current state for recent runs and from the session's log for older ones.

schema.description: Exclusive upper run-id bound from a previous page.

post.description: Returns once the run is accepted — queued behind an active run, or running — not when it finishes. A compacting session holds the request; if the wait runs out the call fails with operationPending and the submission id, and the run still starts later. Retrying with that id cannot start a second run. Follow session events or reread the session.

notifyOnTerminal.description:
Request a terminal emission to the session's immutable
lifecycle controller. It is delivered to a running controller, which may
hear it more than once; others reconcile through `session/runs/read`.
The destination is derived by the gateway; callers supply only the
controller's opaque dedup token.

submissionId.description:
Client-supplied idempotency key, unique per session. Retrying
`session/runs/start` with the same submission id and the same
source/config/terminal notification returns the original run instead
of starting a second one; reusing a submission id with any of those
inputs changed is rejected. The session recognizes it against queued and
active runs and its most recent 256 terminal runs, so a retry older than
that starts a new run.

get.description: Projects one run from its events. A run past the server's detail limit keeps its opening and its most recent turns and sets earlierEventsOmitted; session/events/read has the rest.

post.description: Approves or rejects pending MCP tool calls on the named active run. Valid decisions apply independently; the run resumes only after every pending approval has a decision. A decision whose wait runs out reports status pending and can still apply.
Requests cancellation of the named queued or active run and returns its summary; observe session events for terminal completion. In-flight model and tool activity is aborted; no grace turn runs.

Injects input into the named active run; the model sees it at the next turn boundary without interrupting the in-flight turn. A parked run holds it without waking. Rejected for queued, cancelling, or finished runs. Supply submissionId so a retry lands once; a wait that runs out fails with operationPending and the steering can still land.

schema.description:
The run to steer. Must be the session's current active run, running or
parked; a queued, finished or cancelling run is rejected so a late steer
never lands on the next run.

items.description:
Steering input, same vocabulary as run input. Delivered to the model
at the next turn boundary of the run; it does not interrupt the
in-flight turn or wake a parked run. If the run fails before that
boundary, the input still enters context and the next run sees it as
history. Cancelling the run drops it.

submissionId.description:
Client-supplied idempotency key. Retrying with the same id and the same items
lands the steering once and returns its original id; reusing the id with other
items is rejected. The run recognizes it among its most recent steering batches.

post.description: Moves an unshared root session to universe visibility, one way; its delegated children follow it. Refused on a bot's session, a delegated child, and a session already shared. Core applies it for any caller of the method; who may share is the caller's gate's decision.
post.summary: Share a session with the universe

get.description: Returns separate VFS and environment catalogs with source, reference, availability, readable skill paths, and warnings. Refreshes only when open with no active or queued run, without waking environments. Absent catalogs are omitted.

post.description: Admit or rejoin a requester-scoped audio transcription. The resolved model is immutable. No session or run is created.

idempotencyKey.description:
Scoped to the requester. Matching retries rejoin the original job,
including after defaults change; changed requests conflict. Identity is
retained for the Temporal namespace's workflow-history retention period.

get.description: Read status and transcript text. Caller visibility is enforced by the external gate. Unsubmitted CAS results may expire.

post.description: Cancel unfinished transcription. Repeated cancellation is safe; completed results remain unchanged. Caller ownership is enforced by the external gate.
Validates and stores an immutable filesystem manifest. Upload referenced file blobs first; the returned snapshot ref is content-addressed.

get.description: Returns an immutable snapshot manifest and aggregate file/byte counts; file bodies remain separate blobs.
Lists the mutable universe workspaces with head snapshots, sizes, and revisions.

post.description: Creates a universe workspace attributed to the caller at an optional seed snapshot; absence starts from a server-created empty snapshot.

snapshotRef.description:
Snapshot to seed the workspace from. Absent starts the workspace from
the empty snapshot, committed server-side.

delete.description: Deletes the mutable workspace record; immutable snapshots and blobs remain content-addressed resources.

get.description: Returns workspace metadata, current head snapshot, and revision for safe updates.

patch.description: Moves the workspace head to an existing snapshot, which requires use of the workspace, and updates its display name, which requires configuring it. Pass expectedRevision from a read to prevent lost updates.

get.description: Reads bytes at a path in the current workspace head.
